title: Following an edge link inside the L2 pane keeps the old scroll and drops keyboard focus
body:
## Summary
Clicking a "Who calls it" / "What it reaches" link inside the L2 pane swaps the pane to another component without remounting it, so the pane keeps the previous component's scroll position and the focused link button is removed from the DOM, leaving focus on the body inside an aria-modal dialog.

## Description
Shell renders `<Pane component={open} ...>` with no key (examples/atlas/components/atlas/variants/Shell.tsx:285), and the pane's edge links call `nav.openItem` (examples/atlas/components/atlas/pane/Pane.tsx:256). The same Pane instance re-renders with the new component: its focus effect runs only on mount (Pane.tsx:75-77, deps `[]`), the pane is `overflow-y: auto` (examples/atlas/components/atlas/style/level2/l2-pane.css:29) so scrollTop is kept, and the Link buttons are keyed by the OTHER component (Pane.tsx:188, 199), so the button that held focus unmounts and focus falls to the body. Escape still works through the nav's window listener, but Tab restarts from the top of the document outside the dialog, and the reader lands mid-pane of a component whose header is scrolled away. Technique: accessibility/keyboard-navigation-models ("focus teleports ... after a resort"), async-ui-states/windowing-vs-identifying-keys (an identity change may not keep the previous scroll). The obvious fix, keying the Pane by component id, is a trap: the old instance's useOverlayEscape cleanup schedules a focus-return rAF (examples/demo-kit/src/zoom/useOverlayEscape.ts:105-121) that would pull focus back to the first part AFTER the new pane focused itself. "Fixed" is: on a component change inside one Pane instance, reset scrollTop to 0 and move focus to the pane (or its title), e.g. the focus effect keyed on `component.id`.

## Flow
- open any component (L2), Tab to a link under "What it reaches", press Enter
- nav.openItem -> Pane re-renders with the new component; the focused Link unmounts
- observed: document.activeElement is <body>; the pane's scrollTop is the old one
- fix order: build a DOM render instrument (jsdom or happy-dom) for Pane, seed it red on activeElement and scrollTop, then change Pane's focus effect deps to [component.id] and reset scrollTop

## Expected impact
Keyboard and screen-reader readers who follow the model's edges stay inside the dialog and start at the top of each component. Could break: the return-focus target on close (the opener stays the first part, by the kit's isOpener rule).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - focus stays in the dialog and the new component starts at its top after an in-pane link
Before: walked: focus on body, scrollTop unchanged (3 cases: a link whose key differs, a link whose from-kind key repeats in the new list, the last link at the pane's bottom)
After: predicted: focus on the pane, scrollTop 0 in all three
Method: simulation - no DOM in node --test (no jsdom/happy-dom in the workspace) and no browser this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a happy-dom (or jsdom) render test of Pane: open component A, focus an edge link, switch to B; assert document.activeElement is inside .at-pane and .at-pane scrollTop is 0 (red on the current tree)

title: The mast clips its switchers and level rail on a phone-width window
body:
## Summary
The mast is one fixed-height, overflow-hidden flex row whose two segmented switchers refuse to shrink, so below roughly 700 px the variant and view switchers alone outgrow the row and the level rail and lens read-out are squeezed to nothing or clipped.

## Description
`.at-mast` is `height: var(--at-mast-h)` (56 px), `overflow: hidden`, flex, no wrap (examples/atlas/components/atlas/style/chrome/mast.css:23-36); every child may shrink (mast.css:38-41) except `.at-switch`, which is `flex-shrink: 0` (mast.css:47-51). Round 7 mounts three variants and the lanes drawing publishes two views, so both switchers render (examples/atlas/components/atlas/Mast.tsx:195, 226): five nowrap buttons at 12 px padding each, plus the brand (nowrap), plus 24 px gaps and 24 px inline padding. At 375 px that exceeds the row before the rail is placed; the rail's <nav> shrinks to zero width and its nowrap buttons overflow into the lens read-out, and whatever passes the right edge is clipped by overflow: hidden. Only the counts have a narrow rule (mast.css @media 720). Technique: app-shell (persistent chrome must survive the narrowest supported viewport). What fixed looks like is a design call: wrap the mast to two rows under --at-bp-narrow, or fold the variant switcher into a menu, or drop the brand's subtitle.

## Flow
- open Atlas in a 375 x 800 window (or the desktop window narrowed to its minimum)
- the mast lays out brand, Lanes/Signal/Editorial, Lanes/Turn, the rail and the lens in one 56 px row
- observed (predicted): the rail and lens are clipped or overlap; the level you are on is not visible

## Expected impact
Anyone reading Atlas on a phone or in a narrow side window keeps the level rail, which is the only visible way back up a level besides Escape. Could break: the 56 px mast height the stage's grid row relies on.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every mast control is visible and reachable at 375 px
Before: predicted from the CSS: 2 non-shrinking switchers (5 buttons) + nowrap brand exceed 375 - 48 px of row; rail width 0
After: unmeasured; depends on the chosen layout
Method: simulation - widths summed from the CSS; no browser this round to measure the rendered row
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

title: Shell chrome sets nine live text roles at 11 px, under the repo's 12 px floor
body:
## Summary
`--at-text-micro` is 0.6875rem (11 px) and nine live shell selectors use it for text a reader must read, including the lens-clear control and the pane's section headings, against the overlay's repo rule "no text under 12px".

## Description
The token is declared at examples/atlas/components/atlas/style/base/tokens.css:68. Live consumers in this context: `.at-part` and `.at-cite` (sheet.css:68, 98), `.at-claims-group-head` (sheet.css:145), `.at-rail-sep` (mast.css:129), `.at-lens-clear` - a control - (mast.css:195), `.at-mast-counts` (mast.css:209), `.at-pane-section-head` (l2-pane.css:103), `.at-link-kind` (l2-pane.css:190), `.at-adr-n` (l2-pane.css:211); the lanes variant spends it four more times (lanes.css:150, 171, 678, 810). `.at-part` carries every part number and the pane's layer/system kicker, and `.at-cite` every repository path, so the small size lands on exactly the ids a reader copies. Raising the step to 0.75rem changes the mast's and the claims rail's density (the mast is a fixed 56 px row and already clips on narrow screens, see the sibling card), so it is a design call, not a token swap. Technique: design-tokens/density-and-scale-axes (a type floor is a property of the scale, not of a call site). Sibling card for the lanes drawing: "Screen-space lane chrome is set in world type".

## Flow
- read tokens.css's type ramp: micro 11 px, label 13 px
- grep var(--at-text-micro) in the shell's stylesheets: 9 live selectors
- proposal: raise --at-text-micro to 0.75rem, or retire it in favour of --at-text-label for controls and ids, then look at the mast and rail at 1280 and 720 widths

## Expected impact
Part numbers, paths, pane headings and the lens "clear" control become legible at the size the rest of the repo guarantees. Could break: mast and claims-rail fit; needs a look in the window.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - no shell text under 12 px
Before: 9 live shell selectors at 11 px (plus 4 in the lanes variant)
After: 0 under 12 px if the step is raised; layout effect unmeasured
Method: probe - the selector count is a grep; the visual effect needs the real window, which this round does not have
Result: better
Gate: direction
